notes.title: Devlog#1 presents MoonNews
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/c5224a9842ebe2b5a13c1b58da56462bd3ffc587.png[/img]We are thrilled to extend an invitation for a series of interviews with the dedicated individuals at MoonShell, a pioneering company focused on lunar colonization and exploration. We are excited to initiate this series by conducting our first interview with the remarkable Moritz "Hund" Jung.
Moritz Jung, a renowned entrepreneur, has left his terrestrial businesses and earthly life behind. He embarked on a new journey, obtaining an astropilot license, and is now serving as a manager at MoonShell's lunar base. His transition and experiences promise an intriguing story, and we can't wait to delve into his remarkable journey on the Moon.
We believe that his insights and experiences will not only be enlightening but also inspirational to our audience. We look forward to exploring the intricacies of lunar life, the challenges and opportunities it presents, and the future of lunar colonization through Mr. Jung's perspective.
This interview series aims to shed light on the compelling world of MoonShell and the individuals driving innovation and progress on the lunar frontier. Mr. Jung's story is a testament to the indomitable human spirit and the pursuit of new frontiers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/36b852b554add988b833be146ee05a2d146c3171.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: Good day, Moritz. Thank you for taking the time to speak with us. Let's start with your past. There have been rumors about your involvement in illegal weapon trade during the Resource Wars. Can you comment on this?
Moritz: Well, you know how rumors can be. People like to create stories. I can assure you that there's no official information to support such claims. I've always been focused on the future, not dwelling on the past.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: Your nickname, Hund, has an interesting history. Could you tell us more about its origin?
Moritz: (Chuckles) Ah, the infamous nickname. Back during those chaotic times, I was known for my relentless determination to overcome any obstacles in my way. It's true; I didn't let anything or anyone stand in the way of my goals. Hence, the name.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: Some years ago, you survived an assassination attempt that left you with robotic prosthetics. How has that experience affected you?
Moritz: Surviving that attempt was no small feat, and I've come to appreciate life even more. My prosthetics may make me look like a machine to some, but I'm still very much human. I've learned to be more cautious, but I haven't let it deter me from pursuing my dreams.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: You've been a manager of a European lunar base and a proponent of Martian colonization. Can you tell us more about your ambitions in space exploration?
Moritz: I believe that space exploration is our future. We must expand beyond Earth to ensure the survival of our species. I've always been an advocate for pushing the boundaries of what's possible. Mars colonization is just the beginning, and I aim to be a part of it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: Moritz, I understand your keen interest in the moonshell technology. Could you share what fascinates you the most about it?
Moritz: Moonshell technology is indeed a remarkable development. As a former entrepreneur, what intrigues me the most are the automated workers it has brought to the forefront. These include bots, drones, cargo robots, and construction robots. They have the potential to revolutionize the way we operate on the Moon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/28e6972b95bfaa336895134849114f77e16fdd25.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: That's quite interesting. Let's delve into drones a bit further. Can you tell us about their role and capabilities in the lunar environment?
Moritz: Drones play a crucial role on the Moon. They're flying units used for various purposes, such as resource scanning and terrain analysis. The technology behind these lunar drones is fascinating. They utilize advanced propulsion systems for flight and cutting-edge scanning and imaging technology to assess the lunar surface.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: Could you shed some light on the technology behind their flight and the scanning processes?
Moritz: Certainly. Lunar drones use innovative propulsion systems for mobility in the Moon's low-gravity environment. They often employ energy-efficient engines that provide exceptional thrust and maneuverability. This technology is essential for their smooth operations in lunar missions. In terms of scanning, these drones are equipped with advanced scanners and imaging devices that allow them to analyze resources and thoroughly survey the lunar landscape. They use technology like laser scanning, imaging spectrometry, and X-ray fluorescence to gather essential data for our lunar endeavors. It's a fascinating blend of engineering and science, all contributing to the progress of lunar exploration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/3cd1aaa18754415a36583ad5311d0ebccba40c72.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: Moritz, I'm curious, are all drones on the Moon the same?
Moritz: Not at all. There are various types of drones, each designed for specific purposes. We can either use units specially created for space missions or modify units that previously operated on Earth, perhaps for border surveillance, mining, or even for more nefarious activities like state surveillance by certain governments. Of course, adapting these drones for lunar missions requires advanced technology and the right production facilities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: That's intriguing. The versatility of these drones is remarkable. What else can you tell us about them?
Moritz: Well, what's even more fascinating is that the drone models themselves are just a framework. We can further customize them by adding various modules like Hull, Shield, Engine, Scanners, CPU, Batteries, and AI. These modules can change the drone's parameters, enabling it to perform more complex tasks based on the needs of Moonshell Corporation and lunar colonies. Of course, the more intricate the model and the more modules you add, the longer it takes to manufacture the drone and, consequently, the more expensive it becomes. So, balancing your drone's configuration is crucial because every decision can determine survival or failure on the Moon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: That's a valuable insight, Moritz. So, it's all about optimizing the drone models and their modules to match the demands while considering cost and production time.
Moritz: Exactly. It's a delicate balance, and the right configuration can mean the difference between success and failure on the lunar frontier.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: You said there are also bots, cargo drones, and construction bots. Could you tell us more about them?
Moritz: Certainly, these automated units, bots, cargo drones, and construction bots, function in a similar way. We can create them based on different models and configure their modules to suit specific needs. Of course, it all depends on the available budget, production capacity, and the technology being used. For example, take the Grabrobotter CZ2, a geodetic probe-collecting bot developed in my home country. It allows you to attach two Hull modules, whereas the more technologically advanced Turkish auto-miner, the Kazma XX3, can only accommodate one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/efa26953ba619b72bc59d0b976c519abfbdd4d82.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: I see, but I'd rather not delve too deeply into these technical details. How about we change the topic and talk about the sense of longing for family and loved ones?
Moritz: Let me end - another thing I love in units it’s that the choice of names can provide us with a glimpse into the history, culture, and technological inspirations behind these units and modules. It's a testament to how intertwined our past is with the present and the future of lunar colonization. For instance, the Filipino construction bot, the Tagabuo ME2, played a significant role in their economic boom, while its Greek counterpart caused a labor market crisis. It's also fascinating how companies name their products. Scanning modules for drones bear the names of renowned optical scientists, Hull modules are named after ancient tanks from World War II, and CPU modules are dedicated to brilliant mathematicians from around the world. Now we can change the topic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: It's no secret that you're a father. What can you tell us about your relationship with your daughter?
Moritz: (Smiles) My daughter means the world to me. She's been prepared to inherit my empire since birth, and I have every confidence in her abilities. She's on the Moon, contributing to our goals. Any suspicions of nepotism are unfounded. She earned her place through hard work and determination.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/5667379a5c34bd562cf4116b3bf1bbeb33f03cc4.png[/img]Interviewer: Thank you for your time, Moritz. We appreciate you sharing your thoughts and experiences with us.
Moritz: You're welcome. It's been a pleasure to speak with you. Let's keep our focus on the future and our endeavors in space exploration.

notes.title: Dark Moon Developer Blog #2
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Welcome to the second Developer Blog in which we talk and present some cool features about our upcoming Dark Moon game! We know a lot of of you were expecting some new info so let’s get started!

First, we would like to apologize for the delay in presenting new information as well as being a bit too quiet over the last couple of months. As you may have guessed we are working from home because of the ongoing pandemic, but thankfully the transition was a smooth one and we have been continuing our hard work ever since. We are confident that the upcoming months will be exciting for everyone as we want to share more and more Dark Moon related materials with you, so we’re definitely looking forward to seeing your comments and suggestions!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/d91df121c8d3c4cbbbb3c2a583cc7e259f71b644.jpg[/img]

Previously we’ve shared some information mostly in the form of concept art (which are so cool!). To make our players understand what is going on in Dark Moon, let's start from the basics by introducing… the world. Note that we are not sharing everything as there will be some surprises during your playthroughs, but this little piece should be an interesting read for all the lore enthusiasts out there.

In year 2035, along with technological advances, mankind discovered faster and more efficient methods of extracting resources from the ground. These resources were mined with high efficiency, and although it was a breakthrough in technology, it led to some political tensions and foreshadowed the exhaustion of Earth's natural resources. A peaceful solution to this situation was the attempt to obtain valuable natural resources from the Moon thanks to the research already carried out at that time.
 
The year 2055 was mainly famous for the devastating climate change and the almost complete depletion of resources, but it was also associated with groundbreaking methods of interplanetary movement. Furthermore, the discovery of advanced and more durable materials coupled with the advanced artificial intelligence systems, enabled the first steps in automatic construction of buildings.

Hope bloomed when the Moon Rush project was launched in 2066, where humanity was able to extract materials from the Moon in a very short and efficient time. After numerous discussions and debates, an international compromise was reached on the exploitation of the Moon's resources. Due to the fact that this is a huge step for humanity, it has been recognized that all countries on Earth will be able to enjoy the lunar benefits. 

Within 6 years, the project turned out to be a gigantic success and a symbol of international collaboration thanks to the independence of Moon Shell (2072) - an organization funded by the project's member states. The Moon Shell Corporation, which is credited with the prototype of the iconic spiders (the mobile Moon bases), maintains all established bases on the Moon to reduce costs. For identification purposes, the Moon Shell crew has their own logo on the suits' patches, and only they have the legal and technical capacity to operate the organisation's equipment. Thanks to this, there is no risk that one country would be able to take control of the entire infrastructure on Earth's only natural satellite.

Even though, thoughts of probably expanding to Mars started to surface, but these talks caused quite a number of controversial discussions where some politicians were against the joint expansion, considering that the resources extracted on the Moon fully met the needs of Earth, so states interested in conquering Mars should act on their own behalf.

Little did they all know that all of their upcoming plans will have to be postponed...

###

There you have it, that’s what had happened prior to the solar explosion that turned the international expansion into a survival mission. Of course, the world of Dark Moon also has interesting concepts of morality, desperate measures to survive, difficult choices etc. which all will be present in the game, but we just didn’t want to spoil too much of the game at this time. Speaking of the world…

In Dark Moon you will encounter various astronauts from various countries that took part in the Moon Rush project. Again, we didn’t want to spoil all available countries right off the bat, so here’s one of the main characters that you will encounter on your journey.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/141fa48128c7b44706b9c18b37a26099cfb0680f.jpg[/img]

The very first character that we would like to introduce in this Dev Blog is Ignatiy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/37229f55ac3a28eb1cfeab3e3dff218d080d2b48.gif[/img]

Ignatiy is a devoted patriot, a speed freak, and he loves to tinker with his machines where his only real obstacle is himself. There is no other person on the Moon who knows more about vehicles than him. Following in the footsteps of his father, Ignatiy loved to race back on Earth, but during one of the races he skidded and caused an accident killing four competitors while losing his right arm in the process. The devastating guilt made Ignatiy decide to cool down and give up on racing entirely. His artificial right hand constantly reminds him to remain calm in stressful situations, a grim keepsake. Looking for new challenges and to give back to society at the same time - he went through the entire process of becoming an astronaut, from the absolute basics to knowing every available lunar machine. He enjoys making difficult decisions, and the adrenaline rush during talks between other countries reminds him of the good old days.

Naturally, you will have to take care of him along your journey as well as being cautious when making any new decisions. Ignatiy is a patriot and wants to leave the Moon in one piece, but if the convoy needs to get rid of some disturbing members of the crew - we’ve got a problem. He’ll also provide you with some extremely valuable bonuses and perks, so let’s try to keep him on our side, shall we?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/fb8bb3bc97077ade1d5b58ea376bac66b0410342.jpg[/img]

While we’re discussing who is on our side - L.U.V. (Lunar Utility Vehicle, or simply Gary for the crew) is going to be our loyal companion to the end.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/1ba5cd07a100d8f50d159cd144d40e24a2bb1926.png[/img]

Put into use in 2072 with the creation of Moon Shell, it is an outdated robot for the current times, but our hero has become attached to its logic and corny jokes, and treats him as a friend. Gary is a companion of the player and it has developed some form of empathy and reasoning of how humans behave - resulting in various pleasant and… unpleasant encounters. Although the player could exchange it for a new model in the past, Gary has become an extremely useful companion, cementing itself as a still operational part of the crew. 

For those of you who don’t know Gary was in the Announcement Trailer!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/3564cb592b1e4c00d522d9a4a5f1f295ce4317a3.gif[/img]

Whew! This concludes our second Dark Moon Development Blog, and once again we would like to apologize for not posting anything new sooner. We’re going full throttle to prepare you some awesome new content, so stay tuned for our upcoming updates! Right, if you enjoy this type of content let us know by leaving a comment, and if you have any questions, feel free to create a thread and we will answer any questions as soon as we are able!

Be sure to include Dark Moon on your wishlist as that little click helps us a TON! Thank you!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1105330/Dark_Moon/

We've got plenty of more content incoming, so stay with us guys as we are speeding things up!

Until next time guys!

notes.title: Dark Moon Developer Blog #1
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone,[/b]

Allow us to welcome you to our very first Developer Blog where we share some interesting insights about Dark Moon's development. This is going to be a series of Dev Blogs that will show you some behind-the-scenes materials, our thought process of how we approach designing new mechanics, and other stuff that usually doesn't end up anywhere else. Without further ado - let's begin!

[h1]Why Dark Moon?[/h1]
Not an often asked question if we are being honest but we felt that it deserves some explanation. After all, it's always nice to know what drives developers to start and finish a project. Dark Moon is a game that we believe will be able to tell a story of loneliness, trust, betrayal, friendship, and most importantly it's going to be fully dependent on the player's choices throughout the adventure. We've always wanted to tell engaging stories and we hope we will be able to deliver an immersive experience about coming back home from the Moon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/35a1fd6fe4ec7983ffeb403b98285cd4623a1c87.jpg[/img]

[h1]Non-linear survival - what does it mean?[/h1]
We're extremely excited to see what kind of decisions the players will make throughout their journey as, you've guessed it, each playthrough will be completely different thanks to random locations and events. If one player decides to venture to Location A and another player will head out to Location A as well - there is an extremely high chance they will meet up with a different group, reach different locations, find different resources, not to mention unpredictable events may occur before the location is even reached and it may completely change the current plan of action. This course of action generates a unique experience for each player. Oh! Remember that adapting to the current situation - is key.

Resources are incredibly scarce and the player must manage each type of resource to survive the long and dangerous journey. Easier said than done as on the lunar road you will meet groups of people who will help you out with their valuable skills in exchange for food and shelter. And you will need their skills, so the player has to manage not only the Mechaplex as a vehicle but also as a base with living and breathing people on board.

Still sounds doable? Let's add rivalries into the mix; your quiet group of engineers becomes mad at you for bringing on board a scientist from a rival nation. You need their technical expertise but you also need a scientist to research a vaccine as two of your crewmembers will die if they don't get that particular medication. Add the impeding, never-ending reach of the Sun and things get really… hot. Always stay on your toes in the world of Dark Moon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/3c8ec6357238dc77558bab4e00db8c5809f2c671.jpg[/img]

We are excited to see what kind of stories will appear before our players and whether we will be able to see a happy ending at the end. Hopefully, we will.

[h1]A companion[/h1]
During our Announcement Trailer you might have seen a tiny little robot circling the astronaut when the Mechaplex was in full view. That was not something exclusive for the trailer, that little robot is your companion that will be your guide and moral support during your adventures. Allow us to introduce [b]Gary[/b], your loyal Dark Moon friend. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36350847/01a7f2771af707135a74adf7059c2e5c79cd0610.jpg[/img]

Just to clarify, Gary's design may be a bit different in the game as the image above was one of many concepts we ran for him. We believe that he has to be mobile and fast, so we ran through a couple of ideas and hopefully we will be able to show you the final look of our little fella quite soon. His role in the game is to, as we mentioned, provide moral support, but we've added something interesting to his repertoire. But, that is for another time.

###

And that's about it for the very first Dark Moon Developer Blog and thank you for reading!

We know that this issue didn't have a lot of fancy materials, but we are just getting started - there is more to come. Yes! Expect more Dev Blogs in the future as we love sharing our development journey with the community. 

We also encourage everyone to join the [b]Dark Moon HQ[/b] on [url=https://discordapp.com/invite/5yQUqQa]Discord[/url] (exclusive content available in the future!)

[b]Don't forget to wishlist Dark Moon on Steam:[/b]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1105330/Dark_Moon/ 

Oh, and social media stuff so you can stay up to date:

Until next time,
Jujubee Team
